boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Peebles' Farm record (September 30-October 2, 1864) in the Richmond-Petersburg Campaign [June 1864-March 1865]. Chaffin's Farm (VA075, September 29-30) is the co-operating movement north of the James. Army-wide returns, raid-wide and multi-action loss totals, and the siege as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Humphreys says the Peebles captures gave the whole line of intrenchment, that Potter was driven back in some confusion, and that a new line was intrenched about a mile from the enemy's on October 2; Lee says Heth drove back the infantry who had broken through on the Squirrel Level road.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The ground gained and the repulse of September 30 are both retained.

open_questions: Parke's, Warren's, Griffin's, Potter's and Willcox's reports (Volume XLII Nos. 187, 121, 127, 207, 189), Meade's report, Hill's and Hampton's reports (Nos. 372, 374) and the compiled returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, later commander of its Second Corps, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; it relies on Meade's, Hancock's, Warren's, Burnside's, Parke's and Wilson's reports and quotes Lee's, Beauregard's and Gordon's despatches, so it is not independent of those families. Gillmore's, Meade's, Hancock's, Burnside's, Wilson's, Hampton's, Stannard's and Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volumes XXXVI (Part 2), XL, XLII and XLVI (Part 1), are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; each volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Lee's telegrams largely relay subordinates' reports. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
